summary: AE+SE demo of Redwood Console focusing on tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Customer concerned about PII handling, KMS integration, and predictable latency. Agreed next steps: send security docs, share recording, schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript: [00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. We got Samir on the line to do the console walkthrough. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: Doing well thanks. We got a hard stop at 3:50, but should be fine. Marcus and Priya on from infra and security.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir here, I'm the solutions engineer. I'll take you through tracing, request logs, and our error analysis flow — show how you'd debug latency and failures end-to-end.

[00:25] Marcus Hill: Quick context: we run patient-facing features, PII is critical, and we have strict residency for some data. We're evaluating hosted vs Dedicated or Private deploys for that reason.
[00:38] Avery Chen: Great — we'll call out the VPC and KMS bits. Quick agenda: 1) tracing UI and spans, 2) request logs / filtering, 3) error analysis + replays, 4) next steps and security docs.

[00:50] Samir Patel: Jumping into the console — first screen is the request table. You can filter by route, model, status code. Note the timestamp and token counts, we show per-request cost estimate as well.
[01:12] Samir Patel: If I click a request row it expands into a trace view. We auto-link the request to the trace so you can see latency broken down by network, batching, model decode windows, etc.
[01:30] Marcus Hill: Are the traces correlated with our ingress logs? We use NewRelic and Datadog currently.

[01:36] Samir Patel: Yes — we support trace-id propagation. You can inject the same trace id from your services and Redwood will append ours. We also export spans to OTLP endpoints if you want to aggregate in Datadog/NewRelic.
[01:52] Priya Desai: How long do request logs live in the hosted plan? We need at least 90 days for audits or longer with enterprise add-on.

[01:58] Avery Chen: Hosted default is 30 days; you can purchase extended retention as an add-on or move to Dedicated/Private which gives configurable retention. We'll include that in the security pack.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: Can you show an error case and how we'd debug?

[02:16] Samir Patel: Sure — here's a failed request (status 500). The top-level trace shows a model timeout at the kernel layer — see the spike around token 120. The console surfaces the model error and the backend stack (approx) and a suggested remediation: reduce sequence length or route to lower-cost model variant.

[02:42] Samir Patel: Note: the transcription sometimes shows kernel names like 'K V cache' we call the KV cache — that's the key-value cache for autoregressive decoding; I see some consoles transcriptions misread that as 'K V cash' in older exports, ha.
[02:58] Marcus Hill: If we see repeated 500s, can we auto-fallback to a compatible model?
[03:02] Samir Patel: Yes — routing policies let you fallback to configured variants. You can set latency SLOs and routing rules: low-latency tier, cost-saver tier, and a compatible fallback map.
[03:18] Lena Ortiz: How about replaying user requests for debugging? We have to be careful with PII when replaying.

[03:24] Samir Patel: We have a replay workflow — requests are replayed into an isolated 'debug' environment. We also support redaction at capture time; you can enable PII filters to mask PHI, and we do not persist sensitive fields if that's configured. We'll share the redaction doc.
[03:40] Priya Desai: KMS — we use AWS KMS; can Redwood use customer-managed keys?

[03:45] Avery Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for some enterprise tiers. We'll include concrete architecture diagrams in the pack.

[03:58] Samir Patel: Back to the trace — you can expand individual spans and see per-span logs, environment details, and the model variant used. We also surface token-level timing to see where latency accumulates during decoding.
[04:20] Samir Patel: Here's an example where batching caused a 200ms tail latency — you can see a batching span and how the batch wait increased due to a spike in concurrent requests.
[04:36] Marcus Hill: Is batching configurable per-route? We don't want large batch waits on interactive endpoints.
[04:40] Samir Patel: Absolutely — per-route batching config and dynamic batching thresholds. You can set max wait and max batch size, or disable batching for interactive routes.
[04:56] Lena Ortiz: Can we get alerts tied to regressions in quality? We care about the output dropping after a quantization change.

[05:02] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize ties into evals — you can register prompt suites and baseline metrics. On deployment we compare outputs and will alert on regressions. We'll show an example in the Optimize tab.
[05:18] Samir Patel: Switching to the error analysis panel — you can group errors by type, route, model version, or even by prompt set. The UI will surface the top failing prompts and sample diffs.
[05:34] Avery Chen: Customers like this because it narrows down root cause — whether it's model drift, tokenization issues, or infra instability.
[05:44] Marcus Hill: Do you keep raw model outputs in logs? For compliance we might only want hashes or diffs.
[05:50] Samir Patel: You can configure what's persisted: full payload, redacted payload, or only hashed identifiers. Retention and access controls can be set per account or per-route.
[06:06] Priya Desai: Access controls — SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[06:09] Avery Chen: Yes — SSO with SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. We'll include a matrix for permissions mapping in the security docs.

[06:20] Samir Patel: Now, live demo — I'll trigger a synthetic error. Watch the trace: you can see the warm vs cold start, the model decode stalls, and the console auto-tags it as 'model timeout'. There's a built-in 're-run' button to replay the request against a different model or configuration.
[06:44] Samir Patel: Rerun created a new request entry with linked trace; note the header shows both request ids and the delta in timing so you can quickly compare.
[06:56] Marcus Hill: That compare UI looks useful. Does the re-run hit production capacity or a dedicated debug pool?
[07:02] Samir Patel: By default re-runs use a debug pool isolated from production to avoid impacting SLOs. For Dedicated customers you can route replays to a non-production pool on your capacity.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: About metrics — do you expose token-level cost breakdowns per customer?
[07:22] Avery Chen: Yes, per-request token counts, per-route cost estimates, and cost allocation tags for multi-tenant billing. The console can export CSVs for chargeback.
[07:36] Samir Patel: Quick note: some transcripts auto-convert 'SOC 2' to 'sock-two' in older speech exports; ignore those in previous meeting notes, we'll send clean docs.
[07:46] Priya Desai: Any PCI/PHI specific guidance?

[07:50] Avery Chen: We have a compliance addendum. For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys and strict retention/redaction rules. We'll attach the compliance checklist.
[08:08] Samir Patel: Showing request logs filtering — you can do boolean queries: status:500 AND model:llama-70b quantized:true. It supports time ranges and custom tags.
[08:26] Marcus Hill: Can we programmatically pull logs? API or S3 export?
[08:30] Samir Patel: Both — logs can be streamed to your S3 or BigQuery, or pulled via the Redwood API with pagination. We also have webhook sinks for near realtime alerts.
[08:44] Lena Ortiz: What's the typical latency for hosted in us-west? We need sub-200ms for short prompts.

[08:50] Avery Chen: Typical token latency depends on model and prompt length; for smaller models we see sub-100ms median for short prompts, larger models vary. We'll share our benchmarks with similar prompt shapes.
[09:06] Samir Patel: Another debugging tool: trace flamegraphs. You can expand the flamegraph to see which subsystem contributed to latency — queue/batch/model/decode/network.
[09:20] Samir Patel: Here's an example where a GC pause on the host caused a 300ms spike; the trace points to the infra span and we can correlate with host metrics.
[09:36] Marcus Hill: For Dedicated, can we ship our own metrics into Redwood to correlate?
[09:40] Samir Patel: Yes — we accept custom span tags and metrics via OTLP, and you can link your hosts with the trace id. That makes root cause much faster.
[09:54] Lena Ortiz: About deployment rollouts — A/B canary?
[09:58] Avery Chen: Console supports canary rollouts by traffic split and automatic rollback if error rates or latency exceed thresholds. You can tie rollouts to eval results in Optimize.
[10:14] Priya Desai: Do we get audit logs for who re-ran requests or downloaded full payloads?
[10:19] Samir Patel: Yes — audit trail captures user actions: who re-ran, who exported logs, and who changed routing. For Dedicated/Private you can forward audit logs to your SIEM.

[10:34] Samir Patel: I'm going to open the Optimize tab quickly — you can see a regression alert here where a quantized model introduced tokenization differences. It surfaces example prompts and a delta score.
[10:50] Samir Patel: If you click into a prompt set we keep baselines and a sample diff viewer so you can quickly approve or rollback the model.
[11:02] Marcus Hill: Any restrictions on model variants with Dedicated? We run some custom fine-tuned weights.

[11:06] Samir Patel: Dedicated supports custom models — you can bring your model artifact and we handle the serving runtime, kernel selection, and quantization profiles. Private can be fully air-gapped if needed.
[11:22] Lena Ortiz: Can you share an example link to the recording or deck?
[11:26] Avery Chen: Yep — we'll share the recording and the slides: https://redwood.example.com/decks/console-tracing and a short recording link — Samir will drop in the chat.
[11:40] Samir Patel: Dropped: https://redwood.example.com/recordings/ff-2025-11-12-tracing-demo
[11:46] Priya Desai: One more security nit — do you support customer SOC2 attestations per account?
[11:50] Avery Chen: We can provide SOC2 reports and have contractual addenda for enterprise customers. We'll include a copy and the compliance matrix in the follow-up.
[12:04] Marcus Hill: Timeline: if we wanted to pilot in mid-November, what takes priority?
[12:10] Avery Chen: Pilot is typical: 2-4 week pilot, define success metrics (latency, cost, quality). We can provision a dedicated pool or use hosted with retention and KMS configs for the pilot.
[12:24] Lena Ortiz: Ok, sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
[12:27] Marcus Hill: We'll need to confirm network egress rules and whether we can open OTLP endpoints. Priya needs to review the KMS plan.
[12:36] Avery Chen: We'll send the network checklist and sample terraform for OTLP plus the security pack. Next call we can do a pilot kickoff with Marcus and infra.
[12:46] Samir Patel: Quick pointer — if you want a scripted sanity check, we have a bench spreadsheet that runs typical prompts and measures latency/cost. I'll include that.
[12:58] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, that bench will help. Anything else?
[13:02] Priya Desai: No, just please redact any PHI in recordings before sharing widely.
[13:08] Avery Chen: Absolutely — we'll ensure the shared recording is redacted and will provide a redaction log. I'll follow up with the security artifacts.
[13:18] Samir Patel: Alright wrapping up — recap of next steps and I'll paste links into the CRM: recording, deck, security pack, bench spreadsheet.
[13:30] Avery Chen: Great — thanks everyone for your time. We'll email the materials and propose the pilot kickoff times. Talk soon.
[13:38] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, bye.
[13:40] Meeting end
